text:
GitHub Copilot Fusion became generally available Oct. 28: model routing with Standard, High and Max effort levels.
Start with one small bug and an existing test; inspect the diff and cost. Source: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-route-and-orchestrate-models-with-github-copilot-fusion/
Follow @layer8culture if you're building with AI.

Copilot Fusion just changed model selection. Here's a one-bug test worth keeping.

What changed: GitHub made Fusion generally available Oct. 28 across supported clients, including Copilot CLI.

What it does: chooses models for the task and can use Single, Cascade or Critique flows. You select Standard, High or Max effort. These are effort levels, not three new models.

Builder value: less manual switching between models, more attention on the brief and the result. You still need acceptance criteria.

Try this week:
1. Choose a small bug with an existing failing test.
2. Update your client; select Fusion Standard where available.
3. Ask for a minimal fix that passes that test, with no unrelated changes.
4. Review the diff and run the test yourself.
5. Record correctness, elapsed time and model cost. If it misses, tighten the brief before increasing effort.

Billing is per model used, at that model's rate. A higher effort level isn't a free upgrade.

Signal: the product is moving from picking a model toward coordinating a workflow. Your job is defining what counts as done.

Save this for your next Copilot experiment.
